test_title: PYST 17 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 18 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question: Which sentence contains a misspelled word?

options.text: Many believed the new millennium would bring great change, but some felt embarrassed when their predictions failed.
He didn't want to embarrass himself at the start of the new millenium.
The celebration of the millennium was truly unforgettable, though it did embarrass a few politicians.
She didn't expect the event to embarrass her during the millennium gala.

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. He didn't want to embarrass himself at the start of the new millenium. .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"millennium"** is misspelled in option 2 as **"millenium"** (missing one 'n').
 
• The correct spelling of the word is **"millennium"**, which has two 'n's.
 
• All other options have no spelling errors, making option 2 the correct choice.

Correct sentence: *He didn't want to embarrass himself at the start of the new **millennium**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Commonly Confused Words:**
 
 
• **Millennium:** Correct spelling for a period of 1,000 years.
 
• **Millenium:** Incorrect spelling, often due to the omission of one 'n'.
 
 
 
• **Tips to Avoid Spelling Errors:**
 
 
• Break the word into syllables (mil-len-ni-um) to help remember the double 'n'.
 
• Practice writing commonly misspelled words to reinforce correct spelling.
